changes.before: If $score is assigned 4 and then 9 before echo $score, what prints?
changes.after: A variable gives a value a name so you can use it again.

before: A PHP variable is written with $ before its name, such as $score. It gives you a name for a value.
= assigns the right-hand value to the variable. A later assignment replaces that value; it does not rename the variable.
Unquoted digits such as 3 are numbers. Double-quoted characters such as "Moon" are text.
echo $score prints the value of the variable. The separate echo "\n" instruction adds a line break.
Expected result: 8 followed by a new line. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A variable gives a value a name so you can use it again.
PHP variable names begin with a dollar sign.
Put 8 in the variable that used to hold 3.
The output is `8`. Echo reads the value the variable holds now.
Point to the last assignment before echo.
